Ambush · Perch · Studio proof, sheet one of one

Six directionsfor the watchfloor

Six complete visual identities for Perch — the console where a human decides whether to let an autonomous swarm isolate a production host. Each one is drawn against the same two screens, the same incident, the same host and the same strings, so that what differs between them is the direction and nothing else.

I

What was wrong, and what changed

The rejected pass

The last palette was derived from hex values already sitting in the project's SVG drawings. Those drawings had been made with stock framework colours, so the system faithfully propagated green-400, amber-500 and cyan-400 onto green-tinted near-blacks, arrived at 66 distinct colours with no rule governing any of them, and then measured contrast ratios on the result until it looked rigorous.

Clean arithmetic on a borrowed palette. The measurement was used to license the colours rather than to interrogate them — which is exactly why it read as templated.

#4ade80 #22c55e #16a34a #34d399 #10b981 #059669 #f59e0b #fbbf24 #facc15 #eab308 #d97706 #22d3ee #06b6d4 #0891b2 #38bdf8 #0ea5e9 #ef4444 #dc2626 #f87171 #ec4899 #a855f7 #8b5cf6 #6366f1 #3b82f6 #64748b #94a3b8 #cbd5e1 #e2e8f0 #0f172a #1e293b #334155

The fence. No direction on this sheet uses one of these, or anything within reach of one; every board prints its own distance table.

What changed

There is no brand yet, so none of these six start from a file. Each starts from a named world the product's own vocabulary already implies — the watch, the ledger, the case, the verdict, the record, the hold, containment, blast radius — and every colour in it has to be a material in that world before it is allowed to be a hex.

The budget is eight chromatic values, once, for everything, plus a neutral ramp; and each value must survive the one-sentence test printed beside it on this sheet. A colour that only decorates was cut.

The honest test is not how far is this from the banned hex. It is can you name the material this colour came from — madder, wax, permanganate, binnacle glass, machine-guard lacquer, a signal-red lens. All 34 chromatic values across the six directions land between 11.1 and 26.6 ΔE00 clear of the fence, and not one of them was aimed there.

What deliberately did not change

The content. All six draw the same hold on IsolateHost for host-ops-1, the same five fixed fields in the same fixed order, the same 58m 37s on the clock, and the same blast radius — network.egress, network.ingress — traced to holds.a.rehearsal.blast_radius.affected_capabilities in the fixture.

The earlier prototype printed network_connectivity and remote_management there. Those strings appear nowhere in the fixture. Every board on this sheet now traces its strings to a fixture path, and each one says so on its own page.

Comparison only works if the content is identical. It is.

II

The axis — how much colour, and what it is attached to

The six do not differ in taste. They differ in how much of the screen is allowed to carry colour, and what that colour is bolted to. That is a measurable quantity, so we measured it rather than describing it.

Each board's two product screens were rendered at 1440 and every pixel converted to CIE L*a*b*. The first bar is the share of those pixels carrying real chroma (C* ≥ 20) — alarm, rank, measurement, the throw. The second is the share carrying warmth without saturation (8 ≤ C* < 20) — lamplight, warm stock, a lit plate. Everything else is neutral.

Read the first bar as the chromatic budget actually spent. Full scale is half of one percent of the screen. That is the whole range the six occupy — every one of them decides the same question, and none of them answers it by turning the volume up.

One caveat, stated rather than buried: this measures the screens in the states drawn. Night Bridge's port lantern and Substrate's seated plate are dark in an unarmed pane, so their live destructive control does not appear in these numbers.

Gallery is a true zero — not a rounding. There is not one chromatic pixel in either of its product screens, which is the whole argument of the direction: if you can see colour, something irreversible is running.

Quiet is the outlier on the second bar and it is not an accident: a third of its screen is lamplit warm surface, because in that world attention is marked by light and consequence is marked by the index. Two different jobs, two different signals.

The world

The live control room — a broadcast gallery: rack metal, black-glass under-monitor displays, and tally lamps.

The palette — every value, and the one thing it means

  • lens-pgm#A50002

    The one colour: a 2900 K tungsten filament through a 620 nm signal-red lens. An irreversible action is running in production right now.

  • lens-hot#FFEEE3

    The same filament with no lens in front of it, clipped to its white-hot core: something is cued and waiting on your take. A luminance, not a hue (C*ab 8.4).

  • lens-off#242221

    An unlit lens — grey plastic sitting in a dark recess, so an off lamp still holds its slot.

  • housing#13100E

    The black-anodised lamp bezel, identical in both themes, because a bezel is bolted to the panel whatever colour the panel is painted.

  • umd#191919

    Under-monitor display glass: black in a dark room and black in a lit one. Its right cell always names the source of what sits under it.

  • room#1D150F/#C1BAB6

    Black-anodised rack metal under a dimmed tungsten — the field the equipment stands in. In light mode, the same paint under a neutral work light.

  • glass#141414/#E8E8E8

    The monitor well where content is actually read, achromatic because a grade-1 monitor is calibrated.

  • ink#E8DAD1/#25211D

    Panel lettering and displayed values — top of a three-step ramp whose floor never drops below 4.5:1 on any surface it lands on.

Type

Archivo Narrow (engraved) · Archivo (said) · IBM Plex Mono (shown)

Archivo was drawn for signage, meant to be read fast and from a distance, and its condensed cut is the DIN-adjacent engraved-plate voice a control room actually speaks in. The split is not human-layer versus machine-layer, which is a software distinction — it is the room's own, and it is a safety rule. Anything ENGRAVED is permanent and cannot be wrong (BLAST RADIUS cut into the metal, PVW on the housing); anything DISPLAYED arrived from somewhere and can be. Engraved text carries a real emboss, a dark lip above and a lit lip below, so it reads as cut rather than printed at every size.

The signature

The two-lamp tally. A black-anodised housing carrying two lenses over two engraved legends. PVW burns white-hot the whole time a hold waits on you; PGM is dark; the take bar's only job is to move the light from one to the other. It runs at three scales — verdict tally, queue gutter, preview — and is drawn in situ in all three states. It survives colour removal by construction: a lit PGM lens is identified by its white-hot core at 14.02:1 against an unlit lens, not by the red field, which alone manages 1.96:1.

Severity without colour

The word, a count (4 of 4), and four meter segments — all achromatic, in all states.

The risk it takes

The most demanding screen in the product contains no colour at all — not no red, but nothing chromatic anywhere. An alarm colour on a decision you have not made yet is a lie about the state of the world; the corollary is worth more than the restraint, because the presence of colour anywhere on screen becomes a one-bit safety signal that costs a tired reader nothing to learn.

The world

Night watchkeeping: the darkened bridge, and the deck log written on it. A panel painted not to glare, as few lamps burning as possible because every lamp costs dark adaptation, the record in ink, and a hinged cover over the switches you must not throw by accident.

The palette — every value, and the one thing it means

  • The night#04100F

    What is outside the glass — the only cold value in the system, the darkest, and the ground every instrument is recessed into.

  • Panel graphite#211E1A

    The painted plate everything is silkscreened onto: one material lit two ways, which is why light mode is not a second theme.

  • Silkscreen bone#F2ECDD

    Every word a human wrote or must read. The log is written in ink, and ink is never coloured.

  • Binnacle · 578 nm#AB8200

    A clock is running against you — the countdown and the dwell, and nothing else.

  • Port · 615 nm#F5703F

    The throw: the irreversible act, in the one place you can commit it and nowhere else in the product.

  • Port well#571D19

    The same lantern at low irradiance — the panel at the edge of the lit recess.

  • Binnacle glass#5B4D35

    Light mode. The compass lamp's filter seen unlit: in daylight you do not see the light, you see the glass.

  • Port glass#663737

    Light mode. The sidelight's filter in daylight — and the live throw, which in a bright room is the darkest, most saturated object on screen.

Type

Barlow Semi Condensed · Barlow · IBM Plex Mono

A transport-signage grotesque that ships a genuine condensed cut in the same family — which is what an instrument panel is: the placard and the silkscreen come off one drawing at two widths. Plex Mono enforces the rule that makes the pane checkable — mono means the machine's own bytes, Barlow means English. Seven rem steps. Fallback: Arial Narrow, which ships on macOS and Windows, so the condensed silhouette survives with nothing installed.

The signature

The guarded throw. A hinged cover over a lit recess. Closed, the plate lies flat over the throw's own footprint and occludes it — there is no disabled button to habituate to. Armed, it turns about a knuckled hinge past vertical and leans back above the throw, foreshortened, its shadow falling down the well. Live, the 615 nm lantern burns behind it. Two positions, and what separates armed from live is the lantern, because that is what actually differs.

Severity without colour

The word, a four-segment bar, and a rail whose weight, pattern and luminance move together — solid at CRITICAL, a 5/4 dash at HIGH, a 2/3 dot at MEDIUM, a hairline at LOW. There is no hue anywhere in the queue.

The risk it takes

There is no green in this system and nothing positive gets a colour at all — not reversible, not attested, not governance healthy — because in a console that can isolate a production host, a green light is a reassurance an operator learns to trust without reading.

The world

The darkened bridge and the one lamp on the chart table. A watch keeps its bridge dark to hold its night vision, and rod vision is achromatic.

The palette — every value, and the one thing it means

  • index#E05E28/#943106

    The only chromatic value in the system: a destructive action is held here, undecided, and this much of its hour is left. Never text, never a fill, never a button.

  • night#171717/#BCB5AD

    The room outside the lamp's throw, and the darkest surface anywhere. Chroma 0.0000 — rod vision carries no colour, so neither does the room.

  • steel#1F1F1F/#C7C0B8

    Instrument chrome: the bars, sidebar, rails and every unselected queue row. Chroma 0.0000.

  • plate#33281E/#ECCFB9

    The one lamplit surface. It carries the record on the verdict pane, and on the Watch it moves to the row you are reading — lamplight marks attention, the index marks consequence.

  • plate-hi#3D3025/#F4D7C4

    The raised band inside the plate: its head and its controls, where the countdown and the grant channel sit.

  • grad#727272/#7A7672

    Graduations, engraved ticks, and the spent part of the index line. A track, never information — the lit part is the information.

  • ink-mid#BAB2A8/#3E332A

    Body, key/value pairs, every daemon-emitted string, and the filled stops of the severity and confidence meters.

  • ink#C9C1B7/#292019

    The sentence you are asked to judge, and the grant's heading. Capped at L* 78.4 — nothing under a hooded lamp reaches white.

Type

IBM Plex Sans · IBM Plex Mono

Two cuts of one superfamily, chosen for kinship rather than charm. Perch needs three voices — an engraved panel label, a read sentence, a daemon-emitted value — and Plex is one of very few families whose Mono is drawn on its Sans's skeleton, so the mono value and the sentence above it are visibly the same object machined twice. The third voice is made without a third family: case, tracking, and a right-aligned label gutter, which is how a Braun legend is actually set. Fallback: Helvetica Neue and SF Mono.

The signature

The index line. A rule at the left edge of anything irreversible and undecided, whose inked length is the time remaining — so a fifteen-row queue self-triages at 97.71 / 97.71 / 63.11 / 13.89 % before a word is read. It carries the five fixed slots as numbered engraved graduations (slot 4's tick is hollow because that slot contains an absence). And it is the grant control: the destructive action has no fill and no frame, its left edge is the same line at double weight, drawn as an open channel until armed, filled once armed, closed at both ends when Enter will record. Colour leaves when you decide: nothing in the permanent record is ever inked.

Severity without colour

A four-stop index meter with filled stops plus the word; confidence a five-stop meter plus the numeral; verification tier a labelled position. All of it achromatic, and the grant's three states are printed on the board a second time under filter: grayscale(1).

The risk it takes

Every operator alive expects red for danger, and the entire chromatic budget goes to machine-guard lacquer instead — because red would have to compete with the reader's memory of every error state they have ever seen, and this mark does not mean error, it means undecided and irreversible.

The world

A glazed porcelain spot plate and the permanganate read on it: the instrument for a titration, which is what the decay substrate actually is.

The palette — every value, and the one thing it means

  • d1#A37488

    A trace has become a reading — live strength 0.125–0.25, four doublings under the alert threshold.

  • d2#9B597F

    0.25–0.5. Three doublings under the alert threshold.

  • d3#8F3E78

    0.5–1. Roughly one deposit's worth of live evidence.

  • d4#7A2970

    1–2. One doubling under: the last band before the swarm would escalate.

  • d5#601964

    At or above the alert threshold 2.0 — the substrate is arguing, and this is the only band that opened a hold.

  • plate#E8E4D0

    The porcelain tile: the one lit instrument face in the room, and the only surface a colour is ever drawn on.

  • bench#0D0A07

    A matte benchtop, faintly warm and measurably neutral at C* 1.5, so any chroma anywhere on the screen is an event.

  • ink#F8F3EC

    Everything the swarm did not measure — severity, the countdown, the verification tier, the destructive control — carried achromatically at 15.6:1.

Type

Source Serif 4 · IBM Plex Mono

No sans-serif exists anywhere in Perch. The product is exactly two kinds of text, a record and a measurement; a record is set in a text face and a measurement in a machine face, and there is nothing left for a neutral grotesque to do. Six rem steps, and the SVG figures use three of the same. Fallback: Iowan Old Style / Charter / Palatino, and SF Mono / Menlo.

The signature

The plate bed. A plate is where a thing becomes true, so exactly two objects in Perch may be lit. The decay ladder is the first: a base-2 axis from the evaporation floor to 8, where one octave is one half-life — and where the hold's 3600 s TTL and the substrate's 3600 s half-life turn out to be one axis, so an undecided hold expires at the exact moment the concentration that opened it has halved. The grant is the second: a recess with a hazard-hatched floor and the plate's own seat line dashed into it, until you arm it and the bone plate seats — three states differing by about 85 L* over the same area, with no tint, no fill and no hue in any of them.

Severity without colour

The word, four achromatic cells, a four-segment rail running the full height of the card at 17.9:1, and the qualifier claimed. Severity is a claim by the requesting agent; concentration is a measurement by the substrate; they are not allowed to share an encoding.

The risk it takes

The alarm colour is not a warning colour and the one lit chromatic object is not the severity. In a field with no other chroma the presence of the stain is already the alarm, so the hue can be chosen for meaning rather than volume — and a claim made by the party requesting the action cannot borrow the encoding that measurement earned.

The world

Adjudication and the permanent record: the docket, the exhibit, the chain of custody, the seal, and the ruled line where a name goes.

The palette — every value, and the one thing it means

  • wax#9E2833

    The seal — the only hue that ever means this can hurt: CRITICAL rank and the destructive direction. Always a fill or a rule, never a word. Identical in both themes, because wax does not change colour when you turn the lights on.

  • indelible#BCA5E0/#4A2F80

    Copying-pencil violet: the operator's own hand. Nothing the machine writes is ever this colour, and arming a grant rules the page in it.

  • adversary#D0AC71/#6A4E0A

    The manila exhibit tab: a string the attacker wrote, quoted and never executed. Drawn as a tab and never a hatch, because hatch means absence here and nothing else.

  • custody#87BFAA/#0E4535

    Verdigris on an old seal: a check that actually ran and agreed.

  • console#141414/#B0B0B0

    The bench: a neutral ramp with a* = b* = 0 and R = G = B on every step in both themes, so it cannot land on a banned neutral however the digits fall — every value on that list carries chroma.

  • record stock#2D261E/#E4D4B8

    The document itself: the only material in the system with any warmth, so which thing is the record is answered pre-attentively, before a label is read. Capped below paper-white at L* 85.5.

Type

IBM Plex Mono (the record) · Public Sans (the console)

A court record is a typed record, so the mono is not a code accent — it is the document's own voice, carrying the headline, the countdown, the recital numerals and the folio. Public Sans is the USWDS gothic drawn for government forms, and it speaks only the annotation. The reflex pairing would have been Inter plus JetBrains Mono; JetBrains Mono is a coder's face, which is the register the client rejected.

The signature

Two ruled lines at the end of every record. The record's own is hatched and stays hatched, because swarm:hold:v1 carries no signature under any condition. Yours is empty and waiting. The grant is not a button: it is a blank signature line under the tallest field in the system — a 570 px block of which 400 px is blank — with your operator id, your full 64-hex key and the signed tuple set small beneath it. And arming rules the page: bare stock, then broken dashes, then solid ruling twice as dense in your own ink. Three states that differ by a quantity of ink, never a tint.

Severity without colour

Rank is how much wax: CRITICAL inked, HIGH struck dry in a 2 px outline, MEDIUM ruled in a 1 px ink outline, LOW nothing but the word — plus the word, plus a four-tick register. Monotone decreasing in greyscale, and the board draws the ramp with the colour removed.

The risk it takes

The loudest element on the most dangerous screen in the product is empty. 400 px of blank warm stock, one rule, one waiting ✕, dominant even at thumbnail scale. The thing this product is waiting for is not a click, it is a signature.

The world

The entomological collection: the cabinet, the drawer, the unit tray, the pin, the taxonomic key, and the determination slip a curator writes, signs and ties under the specimen — never removes; a re-determination is pinned below.

The palette — every value, and the one thing it means

  • Ochre#B6904F

    The human gate — the severity that requires a person, and the two request-carried fields that trip it. Stock, so it does not invert.

  • Madder#C26572

    Irreversible and production-touching: the entomological type-label red, which means there is no second one of these.

  • Verdigris#53AFA5/#0E4A45

    The substrate — accumulated, decaying evidence: lane strength, concentration, thresholds crossed, an executable inverse. Ink inverts because the paper does.

  • Mauveine#CEA1D9/#5E3066

    The human hand — what a person determined, signed, or is being asked to sign. It is what Refuse and Grant share, and the only cool colour on a warm screen.

  • The drawer#241F1B

    The specific dark this world has: stained oak and felt under a low lamp, warm at hue 67°, with no blue cast and nothing glowing.

  • The board#D1CDC2

    Museum board on the bench under a lamp — the value that replaced the banned cream, at L* 82.5.

Type

Libre Caslon Text (italic) · Archivo · IBM Plex Mono

Three faces encode who wrote a string: italic serif is Perch's closed vocabulary, sans is Perch's own prose, mono is a machine literal, and mono under a hatch is a string the adversary wrote. Caslon is here on a historical argument — Linnaean-era natural history was set in it — and is reserved for the twelve threat classes and nothing else. Not a didone display serif, because that is banned look #1 arriving through the front door.

The signature

The pin and the determination slip. One shaft, five heads, five labels in an order that never varies by action type; a filled head is a slot this hold can fill, a hollow head is an absence printed rather than collapsed — and those five heads become a five-dot key riding in every queue row, so this action has no mapped undo is legible before the row is opened. The grant is a slip with act. / det. / sig. / date ruled on it and a madder IRREVERSIBLE tab: blank until armed, arming writes it, the second stroke pins it, and a change of mind pins a new slip below rather than editing the first.

Severity without colour

The word, always; a filled stock chip at CRITICAL and HIGH against no chip at all at MEDIUM and LOW; and a rank numeral (4 · stock, 3 · stock, 2 · no stock, 1 · no stock). The earlier four-bar glyph that inverted under greyscale has been removed.

The risk it takes

There is not one coloured line, border, rail, glow or gradient in the entire system. In a collection the red label is not paint on the drawer but a piece of stock tied to the pin, so the only saturated colour on screen is physically attached to the exact object it describes and nothing else can borrow the alarm.

Every rendered text node on all six boards was walked in a headless browser in both colour schemes, its effective foreground composited against its effective background, and its contrast computed. Zero nodes below 4.5:1 on any board. Two decorative separator glyphs (Colony, Gallery) measured 1.4–2.1:1 and were repointed to an ink token during this review; nothing else was touched.

Gallery's 4.20 is the one number worth explaining rather than defending. Its light monitor well is a true grey at C* 0, by the direction's own rule that a grade-1 monitor is calibrated. No achromatic grey at that lightness can get further from slate-200, because the entire remaining distance is slate's own chroma. It is not the framework value with the digits changed; it is the absence of the thing that makes the framework value what it is. Substrate's 8.03 is the same shape of thing — a near-neutral card in its light theme at C* 2.6, against a tinted framework grey.

Read the same table on chromatic tokens only — the values that carry meaning rather than material — and it never drops below 11.07. All 34 of them sit between 11.07 and 26.57.

V

Where to look, and what happens next

The two that are closest

Gallery and Quiet are the same instinct executed twice. Both hold that a 3am instrument should be achromatic almost everywhere, and both spend their whole budget on one signal.

They differ on what the signal is for. Gallery's red means this is running now — it is a state-of-the-world lamp, and it is dark while the decision is still yours. Quiet's orange means this is undecided and irreversible, and this much of its hour is left — it is a state-of-your-queue mark, and it is lit precisely while the decision is still yours. They are opposites wearing the same restraint: one lights up when you are done, the other goes out.

They also differ in warmth. Gallery is 99.98 % neutral and reads as machined metal; Quiet puts a third of the screen under a lamp and reads as a desk. That is the choice: an instrument, or a place to work.

What to look at first

Open the verdict pane on each board and look only at the grant control. Not the palette. Every direction here can hold a palette; the thing that separates them is whether the control that isolates a production host is a physical object with two positions, or a button with a colour change.

Then run the greyscale toggle above. The specimens and every swatch on this sheet lose their colour together. The directions that survive it are the ones where the safety argument was built into the geometry rather than into the hue — and that is the only property in this whole exercise that a bad monitor at hour nine cannot take away from you.

Last, look at the six specimens as a set, from a metre back. Ask which one you could identify from across the room, and which one you could confuse with a dashboard.

What happens when you pick

The chosen direction stops being a board and becomes the system. That is roughly a day of work, and it is the same day whichever of the six you choose:

1. The palette, type scale and spacing become the token package — named values with their one-sentence meanings attached, dark and light, so the meaning travels with the hex and the next person cannot spend a colour on decoration. 2. The five existing prototypes are re-skinned onto those tokens, with the verdict pane's grant control rebuilt first because it is the only component whose geometry is load-bearing. 3. The gallery is regenerated from the prototypes so the whole surface can be read as one thing.

The five directions you do not pick stay on this sheet. They are not wasted — three of them contain a mechanism worth stealing regardless of which identity wins, and those are named below.

Three mechanisms worth keeping whoever wins

The two-position control (Night Bridge's hinged guard, Gallery's two-lamp tally). Armed versus live is a fact about a physical object, not a change of tint, so it survives colour removal by construction. Whichever direction wins should take this with it.

The depleting index (Quiet). The amount of mark on a row equals the time left on it, so a queue triages itself before a word is read.

The printed absence (Colony's hollow pin head, The Record's hatched unwritten line, Substrate's dashed seat). An unfillable slot renders as an explicit absence instead of collapsing — the single most important rule in the verdict pane, and three directions found three good ways to draw it.

The recommendation

Build Quiet. It is the only direction where the identity, the safety control and the layout are the same object: the index line is the brand mark, it is the destructive control, and its length is the countdown. That is not a motif applied to a product — it is the product's hardest fact drawn once and then reused, which is what a real identity is. It also carries the largest measured margin from the fence (ΔE00 10.55), the tightest chromatic budget after Gallery, and the only light mode on this sheet that is a second considered artefact rather than an inversion.

Take Night Bridge's guarded throw with it. Quiet's grant is the strongest idea in the set and still the least physical thing on its own board.

Studio recommendation · yours to overrule

The strongest argument against it

Substrate is the better idea, and it is not close. It is the only direction whose self-audit changed the shape of the design rather than its hex digits: it noticed that a dark ground with one bright ramp is a stock look no matter how unusual the hue, and moved the colour off the ground entirely onto a lit bone plate inset into the room, so the chroma runs dark-on-light. Nothing else on this sheet does that.

It also makes the sharpest product distinction anyone made — severity is a claim by the agent requesting the action, concentration is a measurement by the substrate, so they are not permitted to share an encoding — and it found that the hold's 3600 s TTL and the substrate's 3600 s half-life are one axis. Its decay ladder is the most beautiful object in the exercise.

If you want the direction that will still be interesting in three years, that is the one. If you want the one that will get a tired person through a shift without a wrong grant, it is Quiet.

This sheet

The frame has no colour of its own. Every neutral here is a true grey with a* = b* = 0, so every chromatic pixel on the page belongs to one of the six directions and none of it belongs to us. Its own light values sit 4.2–4.9 ΔE00 from slate-200 for the same structural reason Gallery's do — that distance is slate's chroma, and we do not have any.

How it was made

Type is rem throughout; there is no px font-size in this file. No webfont is loaded and no request of any kind is made — the specimens are embedded, and the type is set in families that ship with the machine. Measurements were taken from the rendered boards, not from the stylesheets.

Boards

Each board carries its own design plan, its own contrast and ΔE tables, and its own account of what it caught itself doing and changed.
